newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate pension bill vote delayed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate pension bill vote delayed.

text.p: A Brazilian Senate committee Tuesday delayed a vote on the government's pension reform bill until next week at the earliest after members said they wanted more time to study a range of amendments to the legislation.

An aide to Senator Beni Veras, who is in charge of the bill in the upper house, said he believed the vote would take place next week despite the expected absence from Congress of some senators because of a holiday in Brazil's northeast.
"I have been in lots of meetings with the leaders (of political parties) and my feeling is that the bill will be voted (on) next week," he said.

About 160 amendments to the bill have been handed to Veras by fellow senators. His staff would begin work immediately on sorting out those which could be incorporated into the text and those which would have to be voted separately.

The government had hoped the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee would vote on the bill this week, paving the way for a first of two votes on the floor of the upper house before July's recess in Congress.

If approved in the Senate, the bill, which seeks to reverse a growing deficit in the pensions system, will have to go back to the Chamber of Deputies for approval of changes made since it was stripped of its main points in the lower house last year.
Many Congress-watchers say the government does not have enough time before next year's elections to approve the reform. It was sent to parliament two years ago but has run into stiff opposition.
The bill would set a minimum retirement age of 60 for men and 55 for women, link pensions to contributions rather than time served and do away with a range of perks for public sector workers.

Veras' aide said a lot of senators were opposed to a key article of the bill which would scrap the current process of automatically increasing civil service pensions to match gains in salaries for workers.
